title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County on August 11th.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are pending.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

title: EJ WATER RECEIVES GRANT
full_story:
US Department of Agriculture Rural Development Illinois State Director Jesus Ortega announced that farmer-founded EJ Water Cooperative, Inc. received $5,537,000 for construction of a reservoir west of Holland, Illinois.  The new reservoir is one of the critical water upgrades the cooperative is making that will provide access to reliable water for more than 16,000 rural residents across seven counties in rural Illinois.

“Under the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Rollins, USDA is committed to ensuring people in rural Illinois have access to safe, reliable water,” said Ortega.  “This project champions the priority to meet the need for safe, clean water in the American heartland that is essential to rural prosperity.”

The new 48-acre, above-ground side channel reservoir can supply water for six months, replacing the previous reservoir that could supply water for just three days.  The new reservoir is 40 feet deep, and the lower intake structure improves water quality by reducing turbidity and providing a more consistent temperature of the water.

The USDA Rural Development investment in the reservoir includes two loans totaling $4,577,000 and a $960,000 grant.  Funding for the reservoir project was provided through Rural Development’s Water and Waste Disposal Loan and Grant Program.  The program helps rural communities extend and improve water and waste treatment facilities that serve local households and businesses.

The late Delbert Mundt founded EJ Water Cooperative, Inc. in 1989 to help people.  This project is among the initiatives he wanted to accomplish.

“I think Delbert would be smiling if he was here today,” said EJ Water Cooperative, Inc. Chief Executive Officer Bill Teichmiller.  “He was always forward looking.  When we can do something to serve a community, it just makes me feel like we’ve done our job, providing our service to the community as a co-op to help people.”

Currently EJ Water Cooperative, Inc. provides access to reliable water for more than 70,000 rural Americans across 19 counties in Central and Southern Illinois and has more plans to expand plant capacity in the future.  The new reservoir was built as part of plans to continue to meet the growing needs of people in Effingham, Shelby, Cumberland, Fayette, Clay, Christian, and Montgomery counties.

Applications for the Water and Waste Disposal Loan and Grant program are accepted year-round.  Additional information about the program is available online or contact [email protected].

title: SEEKING BIDS
full_story:
Clay County is seeking sealed bids for a used 2016 Ford Utility Interceptor.  Proposal forms are available at the Sheriff’s Office.  This vehicle may be viewed and inspected at the Clay County Sheriff’s Office at 300 Broadway Louisville.

Proposals are to be placed in a sealed envelope marked “2016 Ford Utility Interceptor” and submitted no later than 1:00 pm on May 8th, to the Clay County Sheriff’s Office 300 Broadway/P.O. Box 267 Louisville, IL 62858, at which time all bids will be opened and publicly read aloud.  Sale is subject to County Board approval on May 12th, at 6:00pm.

Equipment is to be sold as is and where is.  Successful bidder shall furnish a bank draft or cashier’s check in the full amount of the bid upon taking possession of equipment no later than May 15th.

The Ford Interceptor has 184,784 miles on it, a 3.7 Engine.  This vehicle was used as a patrol unit until April 2026.  This vehicle has motor and transmission issues and is being sold as is.

The County reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to select and award to the bidder whose bid it is felt is in the best interest of the County.

title: WILHOUR TRAVELING OFFICE HOURS
full_story:

On Wednesday May 13th legislative staff will be available at the Case-Halstead Library in Carlyle, from 9:00 am to 10:30 am, at the Centralia Regional Library from 11:00 am to 12:30 pm, and at the Bryan-Bennett Library in Salem from 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm.

Traveling Office Hours will also be held on Wednesday, May 20th at the Olney Public Library from 1 to 3 pm.

title: ACTION REQUEST
full_story:
Illinois Farm Bureau issued an action request Tuesday urging members to ask their US House representatives to support the farm bill.

The House is expected to consider the proposed Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 this week.

Farmers have gone without the certainty of a new farm bill since 2023.

House GOP leaders cleared a rule for the farm bill after a lengthy Rules Committee hearing Tuesday.

The action request will remain open until a vote comes before the House.

Members can access the action request at ilfb.quorum.us/campaign/161433/

title: PLANNING MEETING
full_story:
The Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) is launching a statewide planning initiative this year aimed at shaping future housing policy and investment decisions across Illinois.

This effort, called the Illinois Housing Blueprint, is designed to help municipalities, state agencies, nonprofit organizations and local leaders better understand how housing connects to regional economic development and community needs.  IHDA says the blueprint will serve as a planning tool to guide targeted, community‑specific housing strategies.

As part of the process, IHDA will host a series of listening sessions across the state.  In our region the meeting will be held on June 18th from 11 to 1 pm in Effingham, to gather public input from residents, housing stakeholders and local officials.  The meeting will be held at Koerner Distributor, at 1601 Pike Avenue.

Illinois residents are encouraged to register in advance for listening sessions at ilhousingblueprint.org/community-outreach.  According to IHDA, community participation is critical to ensuring the blueprint reflects the needs of residents across Illinois and represents both urban and rural perspectives.

IHDA is also collecting feedback through a statewide housing survey available in both English and Spanish.  The survey is open to all Illinois residents and asks participants about housing needs, challenges and community priorities.  The survey can be accessed at arcg.is/1qPjKP1.

title: DUMBBELL RECALL
full_story:
Federal safety officials said about 50,000 dumbbells sold at Walmart have been recalled.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission said the FitRx SmartBell Quick-Select 5 to 52.5 pound Adjustable Dumbbells, made by New York-based Tzumi Electronics should be immediately replaced.  The agency said the weight plates can dislodge from the handle during use, posing an “impact hazard.”  The agency said it received over 115 reports of the plates coming loose.  At least six injuries have been reported, including broken toes, bruises, contusions and lacerations.

The recalled dumbbells are model 8361 and carry serial numbers KK23288361 through KK23388361 and KK207608361 through KK21347836.

The dumbbells adjust from 5 to 52.5 pounds in 2.5 or 5-pound increments.  They are black with red accents and include a molded plastic storage tray.  Walmart sold the dumbbells for about $100 from January through November 2024.

Consumers are advised to stop using the dumbbells immediately and contact Tzumi Electronics for a free replacement.

Tzumi Electronics can also be reached at 866-363-2237 or by email at [email protected].
